subject: maths
question: The difference between the compound interest (compounding annually) and simple interest on a sum at the rate of 30 percent per annum for 2 years is Rs. 3600. What is the sum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given directly by the formula:

Difference = P × (R / 100)²

3600 = P × (30 / 100)²

3600 = P × (9 / 100) ⇒ P = 40000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 40000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 30% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI = Rs. 3600

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2b5620dd21648c6c1e52f210c7ca4bd851c2ceb5f8ed3540bf41c2bb9e7fdff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective Simple Interest rate for 2 years = 30% × 2 = 60%

⇒ Effective Compound Interest rate for 2 years = X + Y + (X × Y) / 100

⇒ Effective CI rate = 30% + 30% + (30 × 30) / 100 % = 69%

⇒ Difference in percentage = 69% − 60% = 9%

⇒ According to the question, 9% of the Principal corresponds to Rs. 3600

⇒ 1% of Principal = 3600 ÷ 9 = 400

⇒ Total Sum (100% Principal) = 400 × 100 = 40000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 40000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective CI rate can be found using successive percentage formula: [2R + (R² ÷ 100)]%. The term (R² ÷ 100)% directly gives the difference between CI and SI in percentage.

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is calculated using the standard formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods, which creates the difference over time.
